stem: Which investigation is most appropriate when the clinical picture suggests IgE-mediated sensitisation rather than a delayed non-IgE-mediated process?

options.text: Routine allergy testing for every non-IgE-mediated presentation
No diagnostic test, with diagnosis based on elimination and re-challenge
Urgent full blood count for thrombocytopaenia

explanation: Skin prick testing is the most appropriate investigation for IgE-mediated sensitisation. It helps support an immediate-type allergic mechanism, whereas non-IgE-mediated allergy is usually diagnosed clinically with elimination and re-challenge when appropriate.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because skin prick testing is used to assess IgE-mediated sensitisation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because routine allergy testing is not appropriate for all non-IgE-mediated presentations.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because this is the approach used when non-IgE-mediated allergy is suspected, not the preferred test for IgE-mediated sensitisation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a full blood count does not confirm IgE-mediated sensitisation and is not the routine investigation for this presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because stool microscopy, culture and sensitivity may help assess infection, but it does not confirm IgE-mediated sensitisation.
